pageCache.pageTitle: The Leading Parent Partnership Award - Nexus School
pageCache.text:
The Leading Parent Partnership Award
This award supports our commitment to working in close partnership with all parents and carers, which is central to our Nexus values.
By strengthening relationships between home and school, we create a supportive, inclusive environment where pupils feel secure, valued and ready to learn. Increased parental involvement is closely linked to improved pupil progress, punctuality, attendance and behaviour.
The framework encourages parents and carers to play an active role in their children’s learning, helping to build confidence, resilience and positive outcomes across all aspects of school life.
At Nexus School, we are using the Leading Parent Partnership Award (LPPA) to further strengthen our approach to partnership working. LPPA is a nationally recognised award that supports school improvement while recognising our commitment to open communication, collaboration and shared responsibility for pupil success.
Through the LPPA, we aim to:

Admissions and Consultations
If you would like your child to attend our school, please see full details of our admission arrangements below. Please note that this process applies to any admission, for any year group and in-year admissions will also be considered.
Policy and Procedure
Nexus welcomes any parent who wishes to know more about the school and encourages visits of parents by appointment. Discussion will be informal and a conducted tour of the building will be offered.by a member of the school's Senior Leadership Team.
Although the school offers introductory visits on the above basis, parents are advised that the admission of children with Education Health and Care Plans to schools is a matter for the LA who has statutory responsibility for arranging their provision. There are admissions criteria for each special school that are applied in order to determine if a particular special school would be a suitable placement. Admissions and referrals are dealt with by the Area Education Office (Special Educational Needs Department) in consultation with the school. An admissions panel is held each week at the Area Education Office and admissions are subject to assessment recommendations of the statutory process under the terms of the 1981 Education Act. Under the Code of Practice which came into effect from 1 September 2014, parents of a child who has a Statement of Special Educational Needs / Education Health and Care Plan are entitled to express a preference for any school,mainstream or special, which is in the maintained (state) sector. Nexus School is such a school and provided that the following conditions are met the LA must comply with the parental preferences.
The right of parents to have their preference accepted is not reliant on where they live. Parents who do not live within the Kent County boundary may still express a preference for Nexus School when asked by their LA for their view on an appropriate school to meet their child’s needs.
If the LA decides that one or more of the three conditions set out above are not met by the parental preference they may name an alternative school. When this happens parents should be fully consulted and involved in detailed discussions. If parents are not satisfied with the Education Health and Care Plan (EHCP), including the school which the LA has named, they have the right of appeal to a Tribunal whose decision is final.
The admission of children with Statements of SEN / Education Health and Care Plans to schools is a matter for the LA who has statutory responsibility for arranging their provision. There are admissions criteria for each special school that are applied in order to determine if a particular special school would be a suitable placement. There are over-subscription criteria for Kent Special Schools as the LA has a statutory duty to allocate school places. Special schools do not hold waiting lists.
A link to the admissions criteria for Kent special schools can be found below:
https://www.kelsi.org.uk/admissions/sen-admission-criteria
The named officer in the relevant Area Education Office explains the arrangements for admission to parents and carers as part of the statutory assessment process or as part of any school transition process but further advice is available directly from the Area Offices:
East Kent 03000 421160, SENEast@kent.gov.uk
North Kent 03000 419345, SENNorth@kent.gov.uk
West Kent 03000 420997, SENWest@kent.gov.uk
South Kent 03000 420889, SENSouth@kent.gov.uk

Transport Support
If you are looking to apply for transport for your child to attend Nexus, this page will guide you through the process and provide the support you may need. Understanding how school transport works, who to contact, and how to apply is important to ensure your child can travel safely and reliably.
How to Apply for Transport
School transport applications are managed by Kent County Council. If your child is eligible, you can apply online through their website. The process includes guidance on eligibility, routes, and any special requirements your child may have.
To start your application, visit the Kent Transport website. This site provides step-by-step instructions, important deadlines, and answers to frequently asked questions.
Support from Kent Client Transport Team
We understand that transport arrangements can sometimes be complex. If you have questions, need help with the application, or require support for your child’s journey, the Kent Client Transport Team is here to help.
You can contact them directly via email at: client.transport@kent.gov.uk.

pageCache.pageTitle: Knole Visit to Amazon Warehouse - News - Nexus School
pageCache.text:
Knole Visit to Amazon Warehouse
Tour to Amazon Warehouse
The Knole Class from Post 16 recently visited an Amazon warehouse to learn more about how it operates. It was a great opportunity for us as young adults to see what it is like to work at Amazon and to understand how different roles fit together.
During the visit, we were shown the full process of how items are picked, packed, and shipped to customers. The staff explained each step clearly and showed us how teamwork and organisation are important in making everything run smoothly.
We really enjoyed the visit and found it very interesting to see how such a large workplace functions. It was a valuable experience that helped us learn more about the world of work and possible jobopportunities in the future.
This article has been written by a student in Knole Class.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ightam Visit To Barnes Lodge Care Home - News - Nexus School
pageCache.text:
Ightam Visit To Barnes Lodge Care Home
On 22nd of April, Ightham class visited the Barnes Lodge Care Home in Tonbridge. The purpose of the visit was to meet and socialise with the residents, the average age for moving into a care home is 85–94 (44% of residents), with a significant portion also entering between 75–84. While generally designed for older adults (65+), care homes can accommodate individuals over 18 with specific needs. The majority ofresidents are aged 85 or older.
To break up their day, a few of us decided to sing some old tunes that they might want to sing along to. Another pupil sang a number of songs including Sweet Caroline and I sang Sky Full Of Stars, all of the songs were very much appreciated.
Our visit was also an opportunity for us to consider Barnes Lodge as a place of work. For the 1st time Barnes Lodge is opening its doors to Nexus students and giving them the chance to work alongside residents and staff.
We look forward to developing this important relationship between Nexus and Barnes Lodge.
-Written by a student in Ightam Class

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Experience at Patch Farm - News - Nexus School
pageCache.text:
Our Experience at Patch Farm
Knole and Ightham classes had a fantastic time working at Patch Farm. The experience was both enjoyable and rewarding, and we are very grateful to the team there for welcoming us so warmly. We hope to return in the future so we can continue helping out and building our skills.
During our time on the farm, we carried out a range of tasks, including weeding, raking, planting seeds, and preparing planting beds. These activities gave us a real insight into the hard work involved in farming and helped us to better understand what the job involves on a daily basis.
One of the most rewarding parts of the experience was sowing seeds and then seeing them begin to grow. It was exciting to see the results of our hard work and to feel that we had contributed to something meaningful. The farm itself is a beautiful environment, and after completing our tasks, we were given a tour, including areas at the back of the farm.
I am sure everyone in the group would agree that this was a valuable and enjoyable experience. We all learned new skills.
-Written by a student in Ightam Class

Hillfest Preparations
Hillfest Preparations Are Underway!
This week, some of our students have been busy preparing for the annual performing arts festival competition, Hillfest, which will take place on 3rd July at Tonbridge Castle on the main stage.
We are delighted that 32 students will be representing the school at this fantastic event. Students from across all pathways will be taking part, competing in either singing or dancing performances.
The Dance Club has been working hard on a musical theatre dance inspired by Aladdin. With costumes now ready to go, thanks to the wonderful support of Clare Moriarty, the students are excited to showcase their talents and bring plenty of smiles to the audience.
Meanwhile, some of our talented artists will also be entering the Hillfest Art Competition, creating pieces based on an “Under the Sea” theme.
We look forward to sharing the results and celebrating our students’ achievements after the event.
Vicky would like to extend a heartfelt thank you to all the staff and parents for their support in helping students prepare for Hillfest. Your encouragement and commitment are greatly appreciated.
We wish all of our performers and artists the very best of luck. Have a fantastic time and enjoy this wonderful opportunity to shine!

pageCache.pageTitle: Cirdan Trust Boat Expedition - News - Nexus School
pageCache.text:
Cirdan Trust Boat Expedition
As part of their work towards gold duke of Edinburgh. These students participated in 5 days of sailing starting Poole Harbour. Everyone on board had a wonderful time, with particular highlights of the trip include watching England vs Ghana on the deck of the boat, going to the beach in Cowes (isle of Wight) and having a BBQ or celebrating a students birthday one evening on the deck of the boat.
All students worked incredibly hard to manage the challenges on the way from feeling sea sick to cooking all meals and evening helping to sail the boat. The students completed 75 miles of sailing while they were away and all gained the start yachting qualification. Some students will soon be able to use this to soon complete their Gold Duke of Edinburgh. Well Done everyone the staff and crew of the boat were very impressed with the students hard work and resilience.
